docs.title: iOS Push Delivery Notes
docs.text:
The iOS push path that was verified on 2026-06-06 is:

  1. the app registers an Expo push token on the physical iPhone
  2. the app saves that token to /birds/users/{external_id}
  3. the backend stores it in users.push_token
  4. the Celery worker detects new species for that user
  5. the notification dispatcher posts to Expo Push API
  6. Expo forwards to APNs using the EAS-managed push credentials for the app bundle id
  7. APNs delivers the notification to the iPhone

Important operational notes:

  • a saved Expo push token in Postgres does not guarantee iOS delivery on its own
  • Expo/EAS must also have valid APNs credentials for:
  • com.anonymous.my-bird-app
  • if those APNs credentials are missing, Expo returns:
  • InvalidCredentials
  • Could not find APNs credentials ...

Useful verification commands:

Check that the app saved the push token:

select external_id, email, push_token, check_interval, is_active
from users
where external_id = 'Ora8tDnihwWQ89L6RjlIk4uSL4H2';

Send a direct Expo test push:

curl -X POST https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to":"ExponentPushToken[REPLACE_ME]",
    "title":"Bird spotted nearby!",
    "body":"Test notification from Bird Platform",
    "data":{"test":true}
  }'

Trigger a real nearby-bird poll:

cd /opt/bird-platform/app/bird-platform/bird-agent
.venv/bin/celery -A nearby_bird_alerts.tasks.celery_app call nearby_bird_alerts.tasks.schedule_all_clusters

Watch the worker:

journalctl -u bird-alerts-worker -n 100 --no-pager -f

The server now logs:

  • when a user has new nearby sightings
  • which notification channels are being used
  • the Expo ticket id returned for accepted push sends

  • media moderation-aware save workflows
  • AI-forward product messaging and bird-detail/local-sightings phrasing that better explains recency and evidence windows to end users

docs.title: Context-Aware Bird Likelihood
docs.text:
The Stage 3 likelihood pipeline adds ecological context to species ranking instead of relying on image evidence alone. Its current engineering foundation includes:

  • bulk eBird/EBD observation ingestion into a dedicated raw evidence layer
  • complete-checklist-aware positive and negative training examples
  • deterministic whole-checklist sampling that avoids splitting one observation event across dataset boundaries
  • stratified hard-negative selection across recent-local, seasonal-local, and seasonal-regional evidence
  • canonical species resolution across historical and current common-name variants
  • temporal and geographic metadata features used alongside species identity
  • geospatial reference-layer preparation for richer habitat and location context
  • LightGBM and logistic-regression training support
  • validation and linkage-coverage gates before promotion
  • versioned model artifacts and registry-backed runtime loading
  • guarded runtime feature projection so serving follows the training feature contract
  • resumable backfills that checkpoint only after a complete checklist has been committed
  • phase-level timing and timeout metrics for evidence queries, candidate selection, and writes

This is an end-to-end ML lifecycle: evidence ingestion, label construction, leakage-aware cohort design, hard-negative sampling, feature engineering, model comparison, evaluation gates, artifact versioning, and controlled inference integration. Stage 3 remains promotion-gated so measured staging quality must be accepted before it replaces a live scoring path.

docs.title: Recent Application Improvements
docs.text:

  • pooled PostgreSQL connection reuse in the main compatibility layer
  • paginated sightings/predictions retrieval for more scalable mobile history browsing
  • infinite-scroll loading on the mobile sightings list

  • guest-mode navigation that keeps users in context and presents sign-in prompts without unnecessary screen transitions

  • Stage 3 contextual bird-likelihood foundations spanning EBD ingestion, complete-checklist labels, stratified hard negatives, canonical species linkage, contextual features, resumable backfills, LightGBM training, evaluation gates, and registry-backed inference

docs.title: Bird Q&A / Retrieval
docs.text:

  • retrieval-augmented generation backed by species metadata and semantic embeddings
  • provider abstraction supporting local and configured hosted-model paths
  • retrieval ranking that grounds generated answers in platform bird knowledge instead of relying only on unconstrained model recall
  • graceful fallback behaviour when a configured AI provider is unavailable

docs.title: Intelligent Nearby Alerts
docs.text:
• per-user alert locations, radii, recency windows, and check intervals
  • geographic clustering so nearby users share eBird lookups instead of producing one external request per user
  • Redis caching for repeated cluster queries
  • durable per-user species deduplication to reduce repeated alerts
  • user-controlled push and email notification preferences
  • multi-channel push, email, and webhook dispatch
  • an idempotent PostgreSQL email outbox with retry scheduling, attempt history, safe error classification, and provider-acceptance tracking

The alert system deliberately uses data-driven scheduling and spatial optimisation rather than machine learning. AI is reserved for problems where learned ranking, classification, or grounded language generation provides measurable value; deterministic mechanisms remain in control of scheduling, deduplication, retries, and delivery state.

docs.text:
This page documents the deployed production architecture and the controlled scaling path for Spark Birds. Local development retains compatible service boundaries so application behaviour can be validated before release.

  • PostgreSQL production database
  • Redis-backed task coordination and caching
  • Firebase Storage for media
  • versioned PyTorch classifier artifacts and LightGBM likelihood models

The goal is:

  • efficient infrastructure use
  • simple operations
  • easy model updates
  • room to grow later

docs.title: Current Production Shape
docs.text:
The current efficient production setup is:

  1. run the FastAPI API and background workers on a Hetzner Linux host
  2. use PostgreSQL as the transactional application database
  3. use Redis for nearby-alert scheduling and shared external-data caching
  4. keep media in Firebase/GCS and return signed URLs through the API
  5. load versioned model artifacts on the backend so model promotion is independent of App Store releases

docs.title: Efficient Infrastructure Recommendation
docs.text:
The deployed one-box topology intentionally uses:

  • one backend service
  • one PostgreSQL database host
  • Firebase/GCS object storage
  • separately supervised API, worker, scheduler, and refresh services

docs.title: Deployment topology
docs.text:
• a suitably sized Hetzner VM for bird-agent
  • Firebase Storage for media
  • PostgreSQL for transactional and workflow state
  • Nginx for HTTPS termination and reverse proxying
  • systemd for service supervision

This is more operationally efficient than prematurely introducing:

  • trying to run inference on phones
  • adding separate vector databases
  • adding Kubernetes
  • adding multiple always-on backend services

docs.text:
The current model artifacts are:

  • bird-agent/models/bird-image-model.pt
  • current local training output:
  • /Volumes/DATA/models/bird-sound-model.pt
  • typical production target path:
  • /opt/bird-platform/models/bird-image-model.pt
  • typical production target path:
  • /opt/bird-platform/models/bird-sound-model.pt

Those are best treated as backend-loaded artifacts.

  • no model conversion needed for mobile
  • simpler updates
  • one model version for all users
  • no app-store release needed when the model changes

docs.text:
Examples:

  • Hetzner cloud VM
  • DigitalOcean Droplet
  • AWS EC2 small instance

Why it fits:

  • efficient and predictable always-on option in many cases
  • easy to store .pt files on local disk
  • easy to run FastAPI with one process manager
  • supports the current PostgreSQL, Redis, worker, and model-serving topology

Tradeoffs:

  • you manage more of the server yourself
  • OS patching and service restarts are your responsibility

docs.title: Option B: Simple app platform
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Render
  • Railway
  • Fly.io

Why it fits:

  • easier deployment than a raw VM
  • logs and restarts are simpler
  • good if you want less server management

Tradeoffs:

  • often more expensive than a minimal VM deployment
  • persistent disk and model file handling need more care
  • SQLite can be awkward on some platforms

docs.title: Repository Deployment Model
docs.text:
The repository's current deployment model is:

  • backend:
  • one small Linux VM
  • API:
  • run bird-agent with uvicorn behind a reverse proxy
  • DB:
  • PostgreSQL with Alembic-owned schema migration
  • media:
  • Firebase Storage
  • model files:

  • simple model loading

docs.title: Production: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
PostgreSQL is the production source of truth for:

  • user and species data
  • sightings, predictions, and community workflows
  • moderation, support, promotions, and entitlements
  • model registry and contextual likelihood data
  • durable notification delivery state

Alembic owns production schema evolution. CI validates migrations against an isolated PostgreSQL service before changes can be merged.

docs.text: Some ingestion utilities, tests, and legacy compatibility paths can still use SQLite-oriented assets. They are not the production application database and must not be treated as the authoritative deployment schema.

docs.title: Bird Q&A RAG Pipeline
docs.text:
The app now includes a bird question-and-answer flow that uses the bird_species table as its knowledge base.

The implementation now lives primarily in:

  • bird-agent/rag.py for retrieval, provider selection, and answer generation
  • bird-agent/main.py for the POST /bird-questions/ask and POST /bird-species-rag/rebuild route entrypoints
  • bird-agent/serializers.py for shared species-field extraction used when serializing matches

At a high level:

  1. each bird_species row is turned into searchable text
  2. the question endpoint retrieves the best matching bird rows
  3. the system returns a short answer plus the top matching birds

docs.text: flowchart TD     A["SQLite `bird_species` table"] --> B["Build bird document text per row Common name Scientific name Family / Order Habitat / Diet Conservation status"]      B --> C{"Retrieval provider"}      C -->|Local| D["BM25 retrieval Build cached bird documents Token scoring over species corpus Rank best matching birds"]      C -->|Local semantic optional| D2["Sentence-transformer retrieval BM25 candidate retrieval Load cached local model Load persisted local semantic embeddings Re-rank top candidates Rank best matching birds"]      C -->|OpenAI optional| E["Embedding pipeline Create / refresh cached embeddings Store in `bird_species_rag_embeddings` Embed user question Cosine similarity search"]      D --> F["Top matching birds"]     D2 --> F     E --> F      G["User asks question in app"] --> H["`POST /bird-questions/ask`"]     H --> C      F --> I{"Answer provider"}      I -->|Local| J["Local answer builder Summarize best match Include habitat / diet / conservation Mention alternative matches"]      I -->|Ollama recommended on Hetzner| J2["Local Ollama service OpenAI-compatible `/v1` API Use retrieved bird matches as context Generate final answer on-box"]      I -->|OpenAI optional| K["LLM answer generation Use top bird matches as context Generate natural language answer"]      J --> L["Response to app Answer Matches Provider info"]     J2 --> L     K --> L      J2 -.if Ollama fails.-> J     K -.if OpenAI fails.-> J     E -.if OpenAI retrieval fails.-> D     D2 -.if semantic retrieval fails.-> D      L --> M["Bird List question panel Show answer Show top bird image Show best matching birds"]

docs.title: Recommended Hetzner Production Path
docs.text:
The current recommended Hetzner production path is:

  • BIRD_RAG_RETRIEVAL_PROVIDER=local-semantic
  • BIRD_RAG_ANSWER_PROVIDER=ollama
  • OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
  • OLLAMA_BIRD_RAG_CHAT_MODEL=gemma3:4b

That means:

  • retrieval uses BM25 candidate retrieval plus MiniLM re-ranking
  • answer generation runs through a local Ollama service on the same box
  • the app still falls back to the local answer builder if Ollama is unavailable

docs.title: Local-Only Default
docs.text:
The backend still supports a fully local no-LLM path:

  • BIRD_RAG_RETRIEVAL_PROVIDER=local
  • BIRD_RAG_ANSWER_PROVIDER=local

That means:

  • retrieval uses cached BM25 matching over the generated bird documents
  • answer generation uses a local summary builder
  • OpenAI quota is not required for the default flow

You can also enable a stronger local-only retrieval mode:

BIRD_RAG_RETRIEVAL_PROVIDER=local-semantic
BIRD_RAG_ANSWER_PROVIDER=local

That path keeps answer generation local, but switches retrieval to BM25 candidate retrieval with a cached sentence-transformers re-ranker and persisted local semantic embeddings.

docs.title: Optional Ollama Answer Path
docs.text:
BIRD_RAG_RETRIEVAL_PROVIDER=local-semantic
BIRD_RAG_ANSWER_PROVIDER=ollama
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
OLLAMA_BIRD_RAG_CHAT_MODEL=gemma3:4b

CPU-only server notes:

  • add swap before relying on Ollama on a 4GB VPS
  • cap Ollama context length:
[Service]
Environment="OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=2048"

docs.title: Optional OpenAI Path
docs.text:
If you want to switch back to OpenAI later:

BIRD_RAG_RETRIEVAL_PROVIDER=openai
BIRD_RAG_ANSWER_PROVIDER=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here

Optional model overrides:

OPENAI_BIRD_RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small
OPENAI_BIRD_RAG_CHAT_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini

docs.title: Graceful Fallback
docs.text:
Even when OpenAI is enabled, the backend now degrades gracefully:

  • if OpenAI retrieval fails, it falls back to local TF-IDF retrieval
  • if OpenAI answer generation fails, it falls back to the local answer builder
  • if local semantic retrieval fails, it falls back to local TF-IDF retrieval

So the app can still return likely bird matches even when API quota or upstream AI availability is a problem.

docs.title: Local Cache Behavior
docs.text:
The local retrieval modes now cache their working data in memory:

  • BM25 retrieval caches the tokenized species documents and a species-content hash
  • local semantic retrieval caches the loaded sentence-transformer model, generated species documents, a persisted local semantic embedding matrix, and a species-content hash

The admin rebuild endpoint:

  • POST /bird-species-rag/rebuild

now clears those in-memory caches before rebuilding, so the next request rehydrates them against the latest bird_species content. When the retrieval provider is local-semantic, the backend also refreshes the persisted local semantic embedding table.

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
User-facing question endpoint:

  • POST /bird-questions/ask

Admin rebuild endpoint:

  • POST /bird-species-rag/rebuild

The question response includes:

  • question
  • answer
  • answer_source
  • retrieval_provider
  • answer_provider
  • warning
  • matches

docs.title: Refactor Notes
docs.text:
The provider logic was intentionally extracted so switching retrieval or answer providers later is a configuration change rather than a rewrite. The rest of the backend should treat the bird-question flow as:

  1. route layer in main.py
  2. retrieval/answer orchestration in rag.py
  3. SQLite species source data from bird_species

docs.title: Matching Data Source
docs.text:
Each bird_species row is currently converted into a document using:

  • common name
  • scientific name
  • family
  • order
  • habitat
  • diet
  • conservation status
  • and the extended descriptive fields used by the species detail flow, such as distribution, breeding notes, nest details, interesting facts, and FAQs

This keeps the first-pass bird Q&A grounded in the structured species catalogue already stored in SQLite.

docs.title: Stage 3 likelihood validation and promotion
docs.text:
• Complete representative training runs using the staging EBD dataset
  • Evaluate LightGBM against logistic-regression baselines using class-aware metrics
  • Validate calibration, geographic generalisation, seasonal behaviour, and species coverage
  • Expand canonical species linkage while preserving taxonomy provenance
  • Add richer geospatial and habitat reference features where they improve measured quality
  • Promote a Stage 3 artifact only after quality, coverage, and runtime compatibility gates pass
  • Monitor inference quality and retain a controlled rollback path after promotion

docs.title: Reliable notification delivery
docs.text:
• Introduce a transactional outbox for nearby-alert email delivery
  • Separate durable email enqueueing from provider delivery
  • Add idempotent email retries with bounded backoff
  • Store email provider acceptance identifiers and safe failure classifications
  • Extend the durable outbox contract to push and webhook delivery
  • Add dead-letter inspection and safe replay tooling
  • Process Resend delivery events and Expo push receipts where delivery evidence is required
  • Add notification health metrics, queue-depth monitoring, and safe replay tooling

docs.title: Product quality and operations
docs.text:
• Expand automated coverage for mobile authentication, guest restrictions, alerts, and admin workflows
  • Add admin controls for SLA policies and report-type configuration
  • Add an audit-log interface for moderation and configuration changes
  • Improve user-facing delivery for support replies and moderation updates
  • Continue accessibility, offline-resilience, and degraded-network testing
  • Add production dashboards for API, database, worker, notification, and model health

docs.title: Longer-Term Direction
docs.text:
• Fuse visual evidence with contextual likelihood signals while keeping model contributions explainable
  • Strengthen audio identification as curated training coverage and evaluation evidence improve
  • Add privacy-conscious personalisation based on a user's location and observation history
  • Introduce richer community reputation and repeat-abuse detection with human oversight
  • Expand ecological analytics for seasonal movement, local diversity, and observation trends
  • Evaluate on-device or offline inference only where latency, privacy, and measured user value justify it
  • Scale worker, database, and inference components independently as real usage requires

docs.title: Engineering Principles
docs.text:
Roadmap decisions follow several constraints:

  • measured model quality before production promotion
  • deterministic systems where machine learning is unnecessary
  • human review for consequential moderation decisions
  • explicit privacy boundaries between internal operations and public documentation
  • incremental architecture that can be observed, tested, and rolled back
  • infrastructure selected for suitability, reliability, maintainability, and efficient resource use

The product direction is a connected wildlife platform combining identification, ecological context, structured observation capture, community participation, responsible AI, and production-grade operational tooling.

docs.title: Sound Ingestion And Training Pipeline
docs.text:
This page documents the current sound ingestion, sound dataset preparation, and sound-classifier training flow.

It started as a xeno-canto ingestion pipeline, and now also includes:

  • Dropbox Definitive MP3 imports
  • xeno-canto training-clip top-up across already-covered species
  • Wikimedia Commons audio import
  • species-labeled sound training dataset preparation
  • first-pass sound-classifier training

Key scripts:

  • bird-agent/download_xeno_canto_sounds.py
  • bird-agent/sync_species_sounds.py
  • bird-agent/sound_rag.py
  • bird-agent/check_bird_sound_ingestion_progress.py
  • bird-agent/query_species_sounds.py
  • bird-agent/backfill_xeno_canto_sound_metadata.py
  • bird-agent/run_next_sound_ingestion.py
  • bird-agent/run_sound_ingestion_loop.py
  • bird-agent/check_sound_ingestion_status.py
  • bird-agent/media.py
  • bird-agent/import_commons_bird_sounds.py
  • bird-agent/ai/prepare_sound_training_data.py
  • bird-agent/ai/import_definitive_mp3_sounds.py
  • bird-agent/ai/train_bird_sound_classifier.py
  • bird-agent/ai/decode_audio.swift
  • sound-training-curation-flow.md

It is intentionally split into:

  • ingestion into canonical app sound fields
  • metadata-first retrieval
  • labeled dataset preparation
  • model training
  • supporting loop and audit scripts

docs.title: Source Strategy
docs.text:
Primary source:

  • xeno-canto

Why it fits:

  • free public bird recording archive
  • searchable API and downloadable file links
  • rich metadata per recording
  • broad global species coverage

Important constraint:

  • licenses are per recording, so ingestion must always keep the original license and attribution metadata with the stored file

Relevant official references:

  • xeno-canto API
  • xeno-canto home
  • example recording pages with license and technical metadata:
  • XC51247
  • XC905260

docs.title: Current Database Shape
docs.text:
The current app-facing fields stay in bird_species:

  • song_audio_url
  • call_audio_url

Those remain the fast selected pointers used by the mobile app.

The current source-of-truth table is:

docs.title: bird_species_sound_sources
docs.text:
Column Type Purpose id INTEGER Primary key bird_species_id INTEGER Foreign key to bird_species source_name TEXT Usually xeno-canto source_recording_id TEXT xeno-canto recording id such as XC905260 source_page_url TEXT Canonical xeno-canto recording page download_url TEXT Original downloadable audio URL from the source storage_path TEXT Internal stored file path, local or Firebase-style audio_role TEXT song or call license_name TEXT Full license string recordist TEXT Original recordist attribution quality_grade TEXT Quality rating such as A or B recording_type TEXT song, alarm call, flight call, etc country TEXT Recording country location TEXT Free-text location recorded_at TEXT Date/time text if available duration_seconds REAL Audio length remarks TEXT Recordist remarks background_species TEXT Other species listed in the recording channels INTEGER Mono/stereo style channel count if known sample_rate_hz INTEGER Audio sampling rate if known is_selected INTEGER 1 when this row is the current chosen exemplar created_at TEXT Insert timestamp updated_at TEXT Update timestamp

Current indexes:

  • unique source_name, source_recording_id, audio_role
  • index on bird_species_id, audio_role
  • index on bird_species_id, is_selected

docs.title: 1. Discovery and download
docs.text:
Base script:

  • bird-agent/download_xeno_canto_sounds.py

Current responsibilities:

  • query xeno-canto by scientific name first
  • fall back to common-name aliases when needed
  • capture raw metadata for selected recordings
  • filter candidates by:
  • allowed license
  • preferred quality
  • preferred recording type
  • reasonable duration
  • download the top selected song and call candidates
  • enrich selected rows from the recording detail pages when needed
  • write rows into bird_species_sound_sources

Current newer capability:

  • --additional-training-clips N
  • download extra song recordings beyond the canonical selected pair
  • store them as training_song
  • keep them non-selected so app playback stays stable

Current newer top-up mode:

  • --top-up-all-species
  • scan the full species table, not just species still missing canonical song/call
  • top up only the training-only clip depth
  • leave selected song / call rows unchanged

This is currently the best path for deepening the training dataset from xeno-canto alone.

docs.title: 1a. Training clip scoring
docs.text:
Extra xeno-canto training clips are no longer chosen only by broad role and raw quality rank.

The downloader now applies a dedicated scoring function:

  • score_training_sound_clip(...)

Current scoring preferences:

  • prefer song recordings over call-like roles
  • prefer quality grades:
  • A
  • then B
  • then lower grades
  • prefer moderate training-friendly durations:
  • roughly 5 to 20 seconds strongest
  • penalize clips with:
  • background_species
  • noisy recordist remarks
  • distant / traffic / wind / overlap style notes
  • penalize weak role hints such as:
  • alarm
  • flight call
  • subsong

This gives the pipeline a more learnable training subset than simply "all available song mp3 files."

Conceptually, the score behaves like:

score =
  quality score
  + song-role preference
  + useful-duration bonus
  - background-species penalty
  - noisy-remarks penalty
  - weak-recording-type penalty

The practical goal is:

  • keep fewer noisy exemplars
  • prefer clearer single-species song recordings
  • raise the average usefulness of training clips before they ever reach the classifier

That scoring is now also used during dataset preparation so the exported training set keeps only the top-scoring clips per species. The full curation step is documented separately in:

  • sound-training-curation-flow.md

docs.title: 1b. Definitive MP3 import
docs.text:
Used to supplement the thin selected sound set with a broader curated local library.

Base script:

  • import_definitive_mp3_sounds.py

Current responsibilities:

  • scan Dropbox Definitive MP3
  • normalize filenames such as:
  • Yellowhammer.1.mp3
  • Long Eared Owl.mp3
  • Canadian Goose.mp3
  • map them onto bird_species.common_name
  • apply a small alias table for known naming variants
  • link or copy matched files into:
  • bird-agent/data/sound-training/{species_id}/definitive/...
  • write:
  • definitive_sound_manifest.json
  • definitive_sound_unmatched.json

docs.title: 1c. Wikimedia Commons audio import
docs.text:
Used to add extra freely licensed training clips from Commons species audio categories.

Base script:

  • import_commons_bird_sounds.py

Current responsibilities:

  • query Commons category pages such as:
  • Category:Audio files of <scientific name>
  • Category:Audio files of <common name>
  • fetch file metadata through the MediaWiki API
  • download supported audio formats currently proven in the trainer path:
  • .mp3
  • .wav
  • store them as non-selected training_song rows
  • retry and continue on 429 Too Many Requests responses instead of aborting the whole run

Important current constraint:

  • Commons often exposes bird audio as .ogg or .flac
  • the current importer intentionally limits itself to formats that fit the present decode/training path cleanly

docs.title: 2. Normalize selected files
docs.text:
Base script:

  • bird-agent/sync_species_sounds.py

Current responsibilities:

  • create canonical filenames such as:
  • {slug}_song.mp3
  • {slug}_call.mp3
  • map the selected source rows back into:
  • bird_species.song_audio_url
  • bird_species.call_audio_url
  • keep the selected metadata row marked with is_selected = 1

docs.title: 3. Audit, retrieval, and backfill
docs.text:
Current scripts:

  • check_bird_sound_ingestion_progress.py
  • query_species_sounds.py
  • backfill_xeno_canto_sound_metadata.py

Current capabilities:

  • species with selected song
  • species with selected call
  • species with candidate recordings but nothing selected
  • species still missing any usable sound
  • counts by license and quality
  • metadata-first retrieval for local sound queries
  • backfill enrichment for older rows that were ingested before detail-page metadata capture was added

docs.title: 3b. Build the labeled sound-training dataset
docs.text:
Base script:

  • prepare_sound_training_data.py

Current responsibilities:

  • read bird_species_sound_sources
  • export per-species training folders
  • include selected-only rows or all ingested rows
  • preserve role separation such as:
  • song
  • call
  • normalize extra training roles into song-like training data:
  • definitive
  • training_song
  • write:
  • species.json
  • sound_training_manifest.json

Current dataset root:

  • bird-agent/data/sound-training

Recommended larger network-backed dataset roots:

  • /Volumes/DATA/sound-training
  • /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all

docs.title: 4. Loop orchestration
docs.text:
Current scripts:

  • run_next_sound_ingestion.py
  • run_sound_ingestion_loop.py
  • check_sound_ingestion_status.py

Current behavior:

  • processes 3 species per batch by default
  • waits 20 seconds between batches by default
  • loads XENO_CANTO_API_KEY from bird-agent/.env
  • pauses on operational issues such as a missing API key

docs.title: 5. Train the sound classifier
docs.text:
Base script:

  • train_bird_sound_classifier.py

Current behavior:

  1. load species folders from the training dataset
  2. enforce a minimum clip threshold per species
  3. split clips per species into train / val / test
  4. decode MP3s to WAV using:
  5. decode_audio.swift
  6. resample and crop in PyTorch
  7. convert waveforms to log-mel spectrogram features
  8. train a CNN classifier
  9. save the artifact to:
  10. bird-sound-model.pt

Important current limitation:

  • the sound inference endpoint is not built yet
  • the mobile app can play and upload sound, but cannot yet call a production /identify-bird-sound route

docs.title: Environment Notes
docs.text:
The sound ingestion scripts are now env-only for the xeno-canto key:

  • XENO_CANTO_API_KEY

Recommended .env form:

XENO_CANTO_API_KEY=your_key_here

Avoid wrapping the value in quotes.

docs.title: Operational Warning
docs.text:
Do not run the bird text-data loop and the sound-ingestion loop at the same time.

Both write to:

  • birds.db

Because SQLite allows only one writer at a time, running both loops together can trigger:

  • database is locked

docs.title: Retrieval Layer
docs.text:
Current retrieval is metadata-first in:

  • sound_rag.py

It currently matches on:

  • species
  • song vs call
  • quality
  • country
  • location
  • remarks
  • background species

Future versions can still add embeddings over:

  • remarks
  • background_species
  • recording_type

docs.title: Training Dataset Shape
docs.text:
Expected structure:

sound-training/
  1/
    species.json
    sound_training_manifest.json
    definitive_sound_manifest.json
    song/
      robin_song.mp3
    call/
      robin_call.mp3
    definitive/
      Robin.mp3
    song/
      robin__xc_123456.mp3

Each species folder is keyed by bird_species.id.

The trainer treats these directories as follows:

  • song -> song
  • call -> call
  • definitive -> song-like training data
  • training_song rows are exported into song-like training coverage through the dataset prep flow

docs.title: Recommended Storage Pattern
docs.text:
To avoid filling local disk, the current recommended setup is:

  • keep the small canonical app playback files local if needed
  • store the larger training-oriented sound inventory on the Windows network share

Recommended network paths:

  • /Volumes/DATA/birds/species/sounds
  • /Volumes/DATA/sound-training
  • /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all

Typical workflow:

  1. xeno-canto top-up into /Volumes/DATA/birds/species/sounds
  2. optional Commons import into /Volumes/DATA/birds/species/sounds
  3. rebuild training dataset into /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all
  4. add Dropbox definitive MP3 files into /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all
  5. train from /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
What is already in place:

  • xeno-canto ingestion
  • canonical song/call sync into bird_species
  • metadata-first retrieval
  • app playback
  • species-labeled sound-training dataset generation
  • Dropbox Definitive MP3 import into the training dataset
  • first-pass sound-classifier training
  • saved sound model artifact

What is not yet in place:

  • backend sound inference helper
  • POST /identify-bird-sound
  • app-side sound identification flow

docs.title: Selection Rules
docs.text:
Current default ranking rules:

  1. prefer scientific-name matches over broad common-name matches
  2. prefer permissive licenses over restrictive ones
  3. prefer quality A, then B
  4. prefer clean song for song_audio_url
  5. prefer clean call, alarm call, or flight call for call_audio_url
  6. reject obvious duplicates
  7. reject soundscapes unless they are the only reasonable candidate

docs.title: Why This Is Not Pure RAG Yet
docs.text:
The first job is ingestion and normalization:

  • find recordings
  • store them safely
  • keep source metadata

RAG becomes useful after that:

  • retrieve the best sound examples
  • answer sound-focused questions
  • explain why a clip is a good match

The current implementation order has become:

  1. source ingestion
  2. metadata table
  3. selected file mapping
  4. metadata backfill
  5. retrieval
  6. optional LLM answer generation

docs.title: Sound Training Curation Flow
docs.text:
This page covers the quality-filtering step that sits between sound ingestion and model training.

Its purpose is simple:

  • score each candidate clip
  • keep only the strongest examples per species
  • export a cleaner training dataset

Key script:

  • bird-agent/ai/prepare_sound_training_data.py

docs.title: Why This Exists
docs.text:
After the xeno-canto top-up work, the project had a deeper sound dataset, but the training pool still mixed:

  • strong clean song recordings
  • weaker or noisy song recordings
  • occasional call-like or mixed-context examples

That meant better clips were being added on top of poorer ones instead of replacing them in the exported training set.

The curation step fixes that by making dataset preparation score-aware.

docs.title: 1. Score every candidate clip
docs.text:
Each ingested sound row gets a training-quality score based on metadata already stored in bird_species_sound_sources.

Current inputs include:

  • quality_grade
  • audio_role
  • recording_type
  • duration_seconds
  • remarks
  • background_species
  • is_selected

Broad intent:

  • reward cleaner song-like recordings
  • penalize noisy, distant, overlapping, or weak-context recordings

docs.title: 2. Preserve the quality signal
docs.text:
The quality distinction is not left only in downloader logic.

During dataset preparation, every exported manifest item now includes:

  • training_quality_score

That makes it visible which files were considered strongest for model training.

docs.title: 3. Rank clips per species
docs.text:
Before files are copied into the dataset, each species' valid source rows are sorted by score.

Higher-ranked clips tend to be:

  • definitive, song, or training_song
  • A or B quality
  • moderate duration
  • free of background species
  • free of noisy remarks

Lower-ranked clips tend to be:

  • call
  • long or awkward duration
  • noisy or overlapping
  • marked with background species

docs.title: 4. Export only the top clips
docs.text:
prepare_sound_training_data.py now keeps only the top-scoring clips per species.

Default behavior:

  • --max-clips-per-species 5

That means the exported dataset is no longer "all available clips." It is now a curated subset intended to be more learnable.

docs.title: Inspect the ranking directly
docs.text:
You can also inspect the current top-ranked clips without exporting files by using:

  • --report-only

That prints a JSON report showing, per species:

  • selected clip ids
  • audio roles
  • source recording ids
  • quality metadata
  • training_quality_score

This is useful when you want to audit whether the heuristic ranking is actually choosing the clips you would expect.

docs.title: 5. Rebuild and retrain
docs.text:
Once the curated dataset is exported:

  1. retrain the sound classifier
  2. compare against the previous baseline
  3. judge whether cleaner clips helped more than raw clip count alone

docs.title: Visual Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["All ingested sound rows<br/>bird_species_sound_sources"] --> B["Resolve storage paths<br/>keep only files that exist"]
    B --> C["Score each clip<br/>quality<br/>role<br/>duration<br/>remarks<br/>background species"]
    C --> D["Rank clips within each species"]
    D --> E["Keep top N clips per species<br/>default N = 5"]
    E --> F["Write curated species folders<br/>species.json + manifest"]
    F --> G["Train sound classifier on cleaner inputs"]

docs.title: Current Scoring Direction
docs.text:
The current scoring is intentionally heuristic rather than ML-driven.

It prefers:

  • definitive
  • song
  • training_song
  • quality A and B
  • roughly 5 to 20 second clips

It penalizes:

  • call
  • alarm and flight call
  • subsong
  • background species
  • noisy remarks like wind, traffic, distant, overlap, or low-volume style notes

docs.title: Practical Effect
docs.text:
This changes dataset preparation from:

  • export everything valid

to:

  • export only the strongest clips per species

That should make the training set:

  • smaller
  • cleaner
  • easier to reason about
  • easier to compare across experiments

cd <path-to-bird-platform>/bird-agent
.venv/bin/python -m ai.prepare_sound_training_data \
  --dataset-root /Volumes/DATA/sound-training-all \
  --uploads-dir /Volumes/DATA \
  --include-unselected \
  --mode copy \
  --max-clips-per-species 5

Example report command:

cd <path-to-bird-platform>/bird-agent

  --report-species-limit 20

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text:
The FastAPI backend provides endpoints for:

  • authentication
  • predictions
  • community sharing, ratings, reactions, and comments
  • bird species
  • bird likelihood scoring
  • image uploads
  • sound uploads
  • analytics
  • AI identification
  • bird question answering

FastAPI also provides interactive Swagger documentation at:

/backend-url/docs

docs.title: Standard Response Pattern
docs.text:
Most endpoints return JSON.

For migrated media, image and audio fields are typically returned as signed Firebase/GCS URLs rather than raw local /uploads/... paths.

docs.title: Protected Endpoints
docs.text:
Most application endpoints require:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Community Endpoints
docs.text:
The community feature is built on top of predictions and adds:

  • POST /predictions/{id}/community
  • DELETE /predictions/{id}/community
  • GET /community-predictions
  • GET /community-predictions/{prediction_id}
  • POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/rating
  • POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/reaction
  • GET /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/comments
  • POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/comments

docs.title: Bird Question Endpoints
docs.text:
The bird question feature currently uses:

  • POST /bird-questions/ask
  • POST /bird-species-rag/rebuild

docs.title: Bird Likelihood Endpoint
docs.text:
The current Stage 1 likelihood endpoint is:

  • GET /bird-likelihood

It now defaults to a Stage 2 statistical score based on recent eBird activity, nearby Spark Birds sightings, distance, seasonality, and historical local month-matched observations. Stage 1 remains available as an explicit baseline mode.

docs.title: GET /bird-likelihood
docs.text:
Returns a bird likelihood score for seeing a species near a chosen location.

This endpoint combines:

  • recent eBird sightings
  • recent Spark Birds community sightings
  • the authenticated user's own sightings
  • distance to nearby evidence
  • seasonal suitability from the species record
  • historical species-month matches stored in local observation history

The default implementation is now the Stage 2 statistical model described in the internal likelihood design notes. It remains explainable, but it uses smoothed probabilities instead of only hard thresholds.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
This endpoint is protected and requires:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text:
• species
  • required
  • common species name such as European Robin
  • lat
  • required
  • latitude to evaluate
  • lng
  • required
  • longitude to evaluate
  • radius_km
  • optional
  • defaults to 10
  • maximum 100
  • model_stage
  • optional
  • defaults to stage_2_statistical
  • accepts:
    • stage_2_statistical
    • stage_1_rule_based

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
GET /bird-likelihood?species=European%20Robin&lat=51.5074&lng=-0.1278&radius_km=10&model_stage=stage_2_statistical
Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "species": "European Robin",
  "likelihood_label": "Very High",
  "likelihood_score": 0.84,
  "total_score": 84,
  "recent_sightings_count": 23,
  "nearest_sighting_km": 0.8,
  "last_seen_days_ago": 1,
  "reason": "Seen 23 times within 10km in the last 7 days, with strong recent local evidence.",
  "model_stage": "stage_2_statistical",
  "ebird_sightings_count": 18,
  "community_sightings_count": 3,
  "user_sightings_count": 2,
  "score_breakdown": {
    "recent_probability": 0.979,
    "recency_probability": 0.895,
    "distance_probability": 0.787,
    "season_probability": 1.0,
    "historical_month_probability": 0.722,
    "source_support_probability": 1.0
  }
}

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
• species
  • normalized species name used for scoring
  • likelihood_label
  • one of Low, Medium, High, Very High
  • likelihood_score
  • normalized 0.0-1.0 score for app display
  • total_score
  • raw 0-100 Stage 1 score
  • recent_sightings_count
  • total matched nearby evidence count across supported sources
  • nearest_sighting_km
  • closest matching sighting distance if evidence exists
  • last_seen_days_ago
  • age in whole days of the freshest evidence if available
  • reason
  • short explanation suitable for app UX
  • model_stage
  • current scoring implementation identifier
  • ebird_sightings_count
  • matched evidence rows from recent eBird observations
  • community_sightings_count
  • matched shared community predictions
  • user_sightings_count
  • matched predictions created by the authenticated user
  • score_breakdown
  • component probabilities used to build the final model output

docs.title: Default: Stage 2 statistical model
docs.text:
Stage 2 is still explainable, but it is no longer purely threshold-based.

It combines smoothed probabilities from:

  • recent local sighting volume
  • freshness of evidence
  • proximity of the nearest sighting
  • species seasonal fit
  • historical local month-matched observations
  • support from eBird, community, and user evidence sources

This gives a more realistic probability surface than Stage 1, especially for:

  • sparse data
  • seasonal species
  • species with moderate but consistent historical local presence

docs.title: Baseline: Stage 1 rule-based model
docs.text:
Stage 1 remains available for comparison:

model_stage=stage_1_rule_based

That version uses fixed explainable score buckets rather than smoothed probabilities.

docs.title: Label Mapping
docs.text:
Both model stages currently map the final 0-100 score to labels like this:

Score Label 0-25 Low 26-50 Medium 51-75 High 76-100 Very High

docs.title: Intended Use
docs.text:
This endpoint is appropriate for:

  • surfacing "what am I likely to see here?" suggestions in the app
  • driving nearby bird recommendation UI
  • providing a baseline before Stage 2 statistical modelling
  • debugging evidence quality through score_breakdown

It is not yet the final machine-learned scientific occurrence model. That comes later in Stage 3.

docs.title: GET /predictions
docs.text:
Returns authenticated prediction history.

If the authenticated user does not have a registered local user record, the backend now fails fast instead of falling back to an unscoped all-predictions query.

Each item includes:

  • prediction fields such as prediction_id, confidence, location, image_url, audio_url, sound_length, and notes
  • raw storage-path fields image_path and audio_path
  • resolved_image_url
  • nested bird_species

Prediction images may be:

  • a signed Firebase/GCS URL for uploaded customer media in image_url
  • a stable storage path in image_path
  • absent/null
  • older legacy values may still appear in historic rows until cleaned up, though the current target is stable Firebase storage paths

The nested bird_species object now also includes:

  • default_image_url
  • song_audio_url
  • call_audio_url
  • additional_image_urls

docs.title: GET /predictions/{id}
docs.text:
Returns a single prediction with the same joined species payload.

This endpoint is owner-scoped and is intended for the current user's own predictions.

docs.title: POST /predictions
docs.text:
Creates a prediction.

Typical payload includes:

  • bird_species_id
  • prediction_type
  • confidence
  • location
  • latitude
  • longitude
  • image_url
  • audio_url
  • sound_length
  • notes

image_url for create now expects either:

  • null
  • an approved prediction image storage path such as predictions/approved/...

Pending uploads and arbitrary signed URLs are rejected by the backend.

docs.title: PUT /predictions/{id}
docs.text:
Updates an existing prediction with the same field set.

When the user changes species in the mobile update flow without choosing a new custom photo, the app now clears the old prediction image path so the UI falls back to the selected species image cleanly.

docs.title: DELETE /predictions/{id}
docs.text:
Deletes the authenticated user's prediction.

Deleting a prediction now also removes any related:

  • community share state
  • community ratings
  • community reactions
  • community comments

docs.title: POST /predictions/{id}/community
docs.text:
Marks one of the current user's predictions as shared to Community.

Behavior:

  • keeps the prediction in the user's local Predictions list
  • makes it visible in GET /community-predictions
  • preserves the original community_shared_at timestamp on re-share

docs.title: DELETE /predictions/{id}/community
docs.text:
Removes a prediction from the community feed without deleting the underlying prediction.

Behavior:

  • local prediction remains in the user's Predictions screen
  • item disappears from the Community screen
  • rating, reaction, and comment history are preserved only while shared data remains queryable through the community flow

docs.title: GET /community-predictions
docs.text:
Returns the shared community feed.

Query params:

  • limit optional, defaults to 20, capped at 50
  • cursor optional opaque cursor returned by the previous page

Response shape:

  • items array of community prediction items
  • next_cursor opaque cursor for the next page, or null
  • has_more boolean

Each item includes:

  • the base prediction fields
  • nested shared_by user metadata
  • community_rating aggregate
  • community_reaction aggregate and current user reaction
  • community_comments.count

The mobile app groups these results by user and sorts them client-side after incremental loading via onEndReached.

docs.title: GET /community-predictions/{prediction_id}
docs.text:
Returns a single community-safe prediction detail payload for a shared post.

Use this endpoint when opening another user's prediction from Community. It avoids the owner-only restrictions of GET /predictions/{id}.

docs.title: POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/rating
docs.text:
Creates or updates the authenticated user's 1-5 star rating for a shared prediction.

The response includes:

  • average
  • count
  • user_rating

docs.title: POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/reaction
docs.text:
Creates, updates, or removes the authenticated user's thumbs-up/down reaction for a shared prediction.

Rules:

  • owners cannot react to their own posts
  • sending the same reaction again removes it

The response includes:

  • likes
  • dislikes
  • user_reaction

docs.title: GET /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/comments
docs.text: Returns the shared prediction's comments, newest first.

docs.title: POST /community-predictions/{prediction_id}/comments
docs.text: Adds a new comment to a shared prediction and returns the new comment plus updated count.

docs.title: Confidence Labels
docs.text: Confidence Label >= 0.8 High confidence < 0.8 Low confidence

docs.title: POST /upload-image
docs.text:
Uploads a user-selected image into Firebase Storage when Firebase is configured.

Response:

  • upload_id
  • storage_path

The backend image upload path no longer returns an immediately usable image_url for prediction saves. Instead it creates a pending moderation object under:

  • predictions/pending/{firebase_uid}/images/...

The mobile app then polls moderation status via:

  • GET /prediction-image-uploads/{upload_id}

The mobile app now prefers direct Firebase client uploads for new prediction images when frontend Firebase configuration is present, and only falls back to this endpoint when needed.

Moderation outcome:

  • approved files are moved to predictions/approved/{firebase_uid}/images/...
  • rejected files are deleted
  • failed moderation writes status: "error" into Firestore for easier debugging

docs.title: GET /prediction-image-uploads/{upload_id}
docs.text:
Returns the current moderation status for a pending image upload.

Response fields:

  • status
  • pending
  • processing
  • approved
  • rejected
  • error
  • image_path when approved
  • image_url when approved
  • reason when rejected or errored

docs.title: POST /upload-sound
docs.text:
Uploads a user-selected sound file into Firebase/GCS when Firebase is configured. If Firebase is not configured, the backend falls back to local /uploads/birds/customer/sounds.

Response:

  • audio_url

The mobile app follows the same pattern here: direct Firebase client upload first, backend upload fallback second.

docs.title: POST /identify-bird-image
docs.text:
Uploads an image and runs server-side bird identification.

Response includes:

  • success
  • image_url
  • predictions
  • model_version
  • model_type

Each prediction includes:

  • bird_species_id
  • common_name
  • scientific_name
  • confidence
  • default_image_url

docs.title: Static and Resolved Media
docs.text:
The backend serves:

  • /uploads/birds/species/images
  • /uploads/birds/others_images
  • /uploads/birds/species/sounds
  • /uploads/birds/customer/images

The /uploads mount follows symlinks so synced gallery media can be served correctly.

For migrated species and prediction media, application endpoints now typically return signed Firebase/GCS URLs instead of direct /uploads/... paths.

docs.title: Cleanup And Historical Recovery
docs.text:
Prediction upload cleanup is now part of normal destructive flows:

  • deleting a prediction removes related uploaded media targets
  • deleting an account removes related uploaded prediction media and upload-tracking documents

For older/historical cleanup, use:

  • bird-agent/cleanup_orphaned_prediction_storage.py

Examples:

# dry run
bird-agent/.venv/bin/python bird-agent/cleanup_orphaned_prediction_storage.py

# apply deletions
bird-agent/.venv/bin/python bird-agent/cleanup_orphaned_prediction_storage.py --apply
